lines.text: Headphones on. {label} comes up in the cans — {r.amb}.
You kill the light and roll. Say the slate, then hold still. Aim for a minute; forty-five clean seconds is enough.

Past the lodge, the old stable wall turns the yard into a chain of courts. Ellery keeps withdrawing behind them: school gables, baths lanterns, then the blind fly tower. Rain finds every roof on the way in.
Basement first. It will be the hardest and I want it behind me.
The key turns. The door is heavier than it looks, the way fire doors are.
The carrier lamp flashes. A clipped squelch snaps from the grille.
White static rises for half a second and cuts cleanly off.
The radio gives a relay click, a breath of hiss, then nothing.
On. Four hundred quid. Maybe if I keep saying it I won't be so scared.
One clean minute. That's all they asked for.
That's one. Eighty quid a room, near enough.
Check it before I count it.
Nothing recorded in here yet.
His log. He hadn't done {room} either.
His log. Same rooms, same order. He started where I did. I can still leave.
On. The guard said the stair light was gone. He was right.
Light off, feet still. Same as it has always been.
That's one. Four to go and then I sign the other box.
Listen back. He would have listened back.
Nothing recorded in here yet.
His log. He still had {room} to do.
His log. Nice hand. Kept his own hours, the guard said.
On.
Roll. It's a room. It has always just been a room.
That's one, and there was nobody in it.
Listen back. Listen properly.
Nothing recorded in here yet.
His log. {room} still wanted its minute.
His log. He was fine. Right up until he wasn't, he was fine.
Three weeks ago a man stood exactly here with better mics than mine and did not finish. I keep wanting to know what he did wrong. There is a reason I want that.
His logs are good. That is the problem. A sloppy log I could dismiss. This is a man who wrote down his floor in dBFS at four in the morning because it was true and it mattered.
Six years he had on me. He would have heard this room before he was in it.
He slated every take. Take three. Take four. Even at the end, when — no. Especially at the end. Slating is what you do instead of panicking.
I have started walking the way he walked. Heel down slow, weight to the outside. I did not decide to do that.
The client did not say he died. The client said the job was incomplete. Those are different sentences and they picked the second one on purpose.

Here is the arithmetic. He was better than me and it got him. So being better is not the axis. Something else is the axis, and I have been walking around inside it for two hours looking for a fault in his mic technique.

It wanted something off him. It got it. I have listened to enough of him tonight to know he had it to give — whatever it was, he had lost somebody, or he could be talked into believing he had, and in this place that is the same thing.
he gave it to me. he gave it and gave it and gave it.
Then he was generous and I am not. I have nothing in me it wants. No sister, no wife, no boy on a bike. I have a job, a torch, and a tape with four minutes of nothing on it, and it can starve.
Nothing in here worth a minute. The order names five rooms and this is not one of them.
On. That's better.
Off.
Headphones on. The room comes up in the cans — the size of it, the drip somewhere, the hum in the walls. [r] again to roll.
Not yet. Off it comes.
No. Levels are set. You don't set a level and walk away — you roll. [r].
Done that one. Clean minute, in the bag. I'm not doing it twice.
Not the chapel. Not yet. You do the chapel last, when the other four are on tape.
The room drops out of the cans. Hold still. Aim for sixty seconds; forty-five clean seconds is enough.
Clean. Enough room tone for the job.
Spoiled. {why[0].toUpperCase()}{why.slice(1)}.
Stopped early. That stays on tape. I still owe them a usable take from this room.
My own knee. That's me on the take. Bloody hell.
I shifted. I actually shifted. Six years and I shifted.
That was me. My jacket, my breathing, me.
That was me. In the room. On the take. Again.
Something moved out there and it was me. Hold still. Actually hold still.
AH— no. No. That was — was that me? Was that me?
...what was that.
That was not the tape. That was not me.
Say it wasn't in the room. Say it out loud. — I can't.
Headphones on. Whatever plays now, the room cannot hear.
End of take.
Nothing recorded in this room.
Somebody's log. {room} still needs tone.
Somebody's log. He was working the same list I am.
It found me. That is going to be on every take from here. / It found me again. {n} now. I am the loudest thing in this building.
There is something on the tape that was not in the room.
No. I really want the basement out of the way while I've still got my legs.
Not yet. I never set the levels — six seconds of test audio and then I can head down to the basement.
It is not under the noise floor. It is at the level of the room, and it always was.
Under the noise floor, and closer up than it was in the last room.
Under the noise floor, coming up. Not a word. Then a word.
Five rooms. I have listened to five rooms.
So did I.
I said that name in a room with nobody in it.
Nobody is expecting you.
That is my sentence. That is my sentence with the ends taken off.
You finish, and you thank it.
And again, four seconds later, at exactly the same level.
A voice in a room is never the same twice.
Take four. Clean.
Take four. Clean.
Take four. Clean.
Minus forty-one. Three times. Not one decibel between them.
The recorder. It has taken the recorder.
Without it I am a man standing in the dark for no money at all. I have to find it. There is no version of the night where I do not find it.
The torch is gone.
Fine. The eyes come up in twenty minutes. They always do. You can work in this — you can just about work in this.
The plan. It has taken the plan out of the bag.
Which is a joke, because the drawings were wrong anyway. Now I have got nothing to be wrong with.
It has taken the radio.
The dead radio. The one thing in the bag that does nothing.
That is not a theft. That is a message, and he has understood it.
There. On the floor, lid open, still running. It has been recording the whole time it had it.
The torch. Still on. Pointing at nothing, the way it was left.
The plan, folded the way I do not fold it.
The radio. Squelching, for nobody. Back on the belt.
You come to on the floor of {roomLabel}, which is not a room you walked into.
{minutes} minutes. I have lost {minutes} minutes and they were not mine to lose.
The bag is open. He goes through it on his knees, in the dark, the way you check for a wallet.
It went that way. I think it went that way. I am going to mark it and I am going to be wrong.
Got it.

The five pages keep the shape you gave them. The recorder is still running on the floor between the three of you. / It is not attacking any more. It is waiting, the recorder still running on the floor between the three of you.
I am still in here. That is what your take proves. Do not hand it the master. / Careful. The sentence it likes best is the sentence where I agreed.
RETURN is missing from too many pages. Something could still be saved, but not cleanly.
Rain, and a long enough walk to think in. The case is still in the back of the van and he keeps checking it is, which is not the same as it being there.
Go through it now. Not at the door with somebody watching me do it.
Under the canopy the rain goes quiet and the bay gets loud. Every drip off the lip comes back off the roller door a beat late.
Good room. Bad night to be standing in a good room doing nothing.
Check the kit. You always check the kit, and you have never once found anything wrong with it.

lines.text: What else.
The bag is still open on the step.
The A-1000 is in the case, in the back, where it has been since Tuesday. I could describe every scratch on the lid.
It will still be in the van when I have stopped thinking about it. That is the trouble with a machine you trust. There is nothing to do about it in advance.
Five rooms, one clean minute each. Forty-five seconds of that is standing still and not breathing on the capsule.
Five minutes of tape. For that they are giving me a building for a night, and the keys, and nobody in it.
Written down like that it sounds like a bargain somebody else came out of well.
They send two people for a job this size. I stopped asking for the second one; he only ever talked over the room.
He has told this to enough people that it comes out the same way every time, which is how you know it is the version he has settled on.
One minute. Uninterrupted. That is the whole job and it is the only rule in it.
Anything that lands inside the minute — a step, a door, my own breath on the capsule — and the minute is gone and I start it again.
The machine does not care whose fault it was. That is the thing I like about it. It is the only part of this that has never once argued.
Cans on, and I am not standing in the room any more. I am inside the machine, listening to the room through it.
People never believe that. You do not hear a building. You hear what your microphone thinks of a building, and you spend the night deciding whether to believe it.
Everything I decide tonight I decide off a meter and a pair of headphones. Write that down and it sounds thin. It has been twenty years.
Batteries. The torch and the deck come out of the same tin, and it is the torch that empties it.
So every minute of light is a minute of tape I might want later. There is no way round that and there never has been.
He checks the spare cells twice, in the dark, by feel — the way you check a thing you have already checked.
A440. Steel. It does not drift, it does not want power, and it does not care what the room thinks of it.
One known thing to carry into rooms that are not. You would be amazed how far that gets you at four in the morning.
And the return. Somebody took a perfectly good interface and rewired it wrong, on purpose, and it does something a right one cannot.
It is not on the inventory. It is not on anybody's inventory. I am not going to be the one who puts it on one.
The set. Check in on the hour, he said. Nobody said what happens if I do not, which I noticed at the time and did not ask about.
It works out here. Everything works out here.
He turns to face the roller door and waits for a gap in the rain.
Testing. One. Ellery, service bay, twenty-two forty.

lines.text: The bay hands it back off the roller door about a beat late, the way a room this shape should.
Long tail on that. Longer than a bay this size has any business having.
Wet steel. Wet steel does that.
He writes nothing down, and does not move for a moment, and then picks the bag up.
